title: Introduce kernel-pulse NVTX ranges and batch-shape profiler
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds opt-in NVTX scopes for kernel pulse regions and a new batch-shape microbenchmark harness with dashboard export; no user-facing API changes.
description: Motivation: profiling gaps around short-lived kernel bursts and the shape of request batches made it hard to correlate scheduler decisions with per-kernel latency and KV-cache hit patterns. This PR instruments fine-grained 'kernel-pulse' NVTX ranges inside the runtime hot path, adds epoch/phase counters, and ships a synthetic batch-shape microbenchmark that can generate representative load (length distributions + concurrency patterns) and export timeline artifacts for the perf dashboard. High-level changes: 1) lightweight scope guard nvtx/KernelPulseScope (C++) + small cross-platform shim under runtime/profiling so feature is compiled behind REDWOOD_ENABLE_NVTX; 2) batch-shape harness (python) that emits JSON/CSV traces and a speedscope-compatible timeline; 3) scheduler hooks to record enqueue/schedule/launch phases as ephemeral counters and attach batch-shape metadata to traces; 4) dashboard export tool that converts microbench traces to our perf-dashboard JSON schema. Commits: (1) add nvtx scope and scoped counter implementation; (2) initial batch-shape generator and runner scripts; (3) export tool + CI job; (4) address review feedback and add unit/integration tests. Files changed (high level): runtime/profiling/nvtx_scope.h, runtime/profiling/nvtx_scope.cc, runtime/telemetry/phase_counters.h, runtime/scheduler/schedule_hooks.cc, tools/microbench/batch_shape_runner.py, tools/microbench/export_to_perf_dashboard.py, tests/microbench/test_shape_runner.py, CI: .github/workflows/microbench.yml, docs/observability/batch_shaping.md. Example snippet added (small): KernelPulseScope k("knet-launch"); // lightweight RAII range. Implementation notes: NVTX integration is opt-in at build/runtime to avoid impacting production unless explicitly enabled. The batch-shape harness can be run locally or in CI with REDWOOD_PROFILE_BATCH_SHAPE=1 and includes a small data generator for synthetic prompt-length distributions. Review conversation summary: Liam requested that NVTX allocation be guarded to avoid linking on platforms without NVTX; addressed by adding a compile-time shim and fallbacks. Priya asked for clearer labels in the exported timeline and a sample speedscope load; addressed and added a sample speedscope payload to tools/microbench/samples/. Diego called out a potential race in the phase counter when a request is canceled; I added an atomic backstop and a unit test that simulates cancellations. CI: first run experienced a flaky integration test (test_shape_runner) due to timing; fixed by adding a deterministic RNG seed and retry harness; subsequent CI pipeline passed (build+unit+microbench export). Performance notes: using the NVTX scopes adds ~50-120ns of overhead per short-lived kernel on x86; measured end-to-end microbench medians show the instrumentation overhead <0.5% under realistic load. Backwards compatibility and rollout: feature gated behind REDWOOD_ENABLE_NVTX and REDWOOD_PROFILE_BATCH_SHAPE; no changes to public APIs; recommended canary: enable harness in perf-canary infra first and validate dashboard export. Merge: PR was approved by all reviewers and squashed/merged on 2024-10-22. Follow-ups: track ENG-1489 to wire batch-shape insights into the console dashboards, and ENG-1423 to add aggregated KV-hit-percentile charts derived from these traces.
